kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore the food of Bolivia, Brazil, and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  This combination lets you compare the food of a major Brazilian city, highland Bolivian cuisine, and Uruguay's parrilla tradition. But on the existing tour, Montevideo is visited on a one-day trip from Buenos Aires, and much of the Bolivian section is devoted to a jeep journey. Restaurants and tastings require free time outside the main sightseeing program.
---

## What the food and wine filter means for these three countries

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The relevant [20-day journey through 6 Latin American countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) includes Brazil, Uruguay, and Bolivia as main destinations, but travelers also visit Argentina and Chile between them and finish in Peru. This is an extended sightseeing itinerary with an additional interest in gastronomy, **not a ready-made series of tastings restricted to the three selected countries**.

The distinctions matter: Uruguay features a one-day ferry excursion to Montevideo, Bolivia has a high-altitude expedition stage, and Brazil includes Rio and Iguaçu. There is no separate included food tour in each of the three countries. You can explore the local cuisine independently during free hours or arrange additional stops in advance. Other combinations are available in the [multi-country food and wine catalog](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Brazil: making time for a restaurant in Rio

Several days in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) are devoted to Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain, and sightseeing around the city. This offers a better opportunity to explore local cuisine independently than the subsequent Iguaçu stage, which involves flights and excursions on both sides of the falls.

For a first introduction to Brazilian food, you might try dishes made with rice and beans, cassava, fish, or tropical fruit. The itinerary does not specify any particular restaurant, cooking class, or tasting menu. If food is your principal reason for traveling, it is worth discussing a free evening in Rio in advance without cutting into the already confirmed city tour.

## Uruguay: fitting Montevideo's food into a single day is difficult

Travelers take a ferry from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). The sightseeing tour includes the port, Independence Square, the old town, and the cathedral, followed by free time before the return journey. It is **the ferry timetable and the length of the guided city tour** that determine whether there will be enough time for a proper lunch.

Uruguayan parrilla is the tradition of grilling meat on a grate over hot coals. Mercado del Puerto, in Montevideo's Old City, is known for places serving local food. However, the existing tour does not list a visit to this market or a Uruguayan wine tasting as a separate activity. Even though the market is conveniently located near the port area, there may not be enough free time, so this needs to be confirmed before deciding to add a meal.

If the purpose of the trip is specifically to enjoy parrilla, local wines, and an unhurried evening, a one-day excursion may feel rushed. An extra night in Uruguay would require changes to the itinerary, ferry tickets, transfers, and accommodation. Also compare [other tours in Uruguay](/uruguay/tour/): simply stopping in the country says nothing about the time devoted to food.

## Bolivia: altitude and roads first, then La Paz cuisine

The Bolivian stage begins after Chile's Atacama Desert. Jeeps travel past high-altitude lagoons and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), then toward the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Parts of the journey take place above 4,000 m, with an overnight stay in expedition-style accommodation. In these conditions, reliable meals and an adequate supply of drinking water take priority over extended restaurant stops.

A city-based introduction to Bolivian cuisine makes more sense in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). The main program includes a city tour, historic neighborhoods, and the Witches' Market, which should not be mistaken for an included food market visit. Dishes featuring potatoes, corn, and Andean grains could provide the basis for a separate dinner if the schedule allows. Those sensitive to altitude may prefer a relaxed addition without extra transfers.

After La Paz, the tour continues through Tiwanaku toward the Peruvian border. A food stop on a border-crossing day requires particularly careful scheduling.

| Stage | What limits food experiences |
|---|---|
| Rio | Sightseeing and the flight to Iguaçu |
| Montevideo | A same-day return ferry |
| Bolivia | Altitude and long road journeys |

## Where is the wine on this itinerary?

On the Chilean section, an optional excursion to wineries in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) includes a tasting. This is a genuine option in the program, but it **costs extra**, takes place outside the Bolivia–Brazil–Uruguay trio, and requires arrangement. Argentina also offers a tango show with dinner, again outside the selected trio.

Uruguayan wines and parrilla are another possible gastronomic theme, but the current itinerary does not include a confirmed winery visit in Uruguay. If wine matters more than the other excursions, compare [food and wine tours in Chile](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/) with the option of modifying the Montevideo program.

## Documents, food in luggage, and planning

Travelers cross an international border between Buenos Aires and Montevideo. Uruguay's sanitary authority restricts the import of certain animal and plant products without the appropriate authorization. Buying delicacies at a market does not mean you can carry them across the next border without checking the rules. Choose clearly labeled products as souvenirs and review the applicable restrictions in advance.

Ada Tours helps you compare the ferry timetable, the day's itinerary, free time, and options for an additional meal. Entry conditions, border procedures, and payment arrangements are checked according to each traveler's citizenship and documents. On an extended journey through 6 countries, one extra gastronomic day can affect several subsequent connections; any changes should be discussed before booking.

The [general Bolivia, Brazil, and Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_uruguay/) lists trips combining this geography with other interests. Choosing the food and wine option makes sense when the actual itinerary provides the desired time to dine, not merely the right country names.

## Frequently asked questions about a food-focused journey

### Is a parrilla meal included in Montevideo?

No. A separate lunch at a parrilla restaurant is not among the confirmed included excursions. It may be possible during free time if the schedule allows, but this needs to be arranged.

### Can we visit Mercado del Puerto during the trip?

The market is in Montevideo's old port district, but a visit is not guaranteed in the itinerary. It depends on the timing of the city tour, restaurant hours, and the return ferry.

### Is there a wine tasting in Bolivia or Uruguay?

The current tour does not confirm dedicated wine excursions in either country. An optional winery visit with tasting takes place in Chile during the Santiago stage.

### When should we plan a separate gastronomic dinner?

The most obvious city opportunities are in Rio and La Paz. Montevideo is constrained by the one-day excursion. Any adjustment must preserve the planned sightseeing, transfers, and necessary connections.

kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Nature in Bolivia, Brazil, and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Iguaçu Falls and Tijuca Forest in Brazil, the lagoons and Uyuni Salt Flat in Bolivia, and a ferry crossing of the Río de la Plata to Uruguay. We compare the real nature stages of the 20-day and 32-day itineraries, explaining where travelers explore cities and where they experience waterfalls and highland landscapes.
---

## Nature in Bolivia, Brazil, and Uruguay: what connects these itineraries?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Both existing trips — [“6 Latin American Countries in 20 Days”](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [“8 South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) — feature [Brazil](/brazil/), [Uruguay](/uruguay/), and [Bolivia](/bolivia/) as main countries. However, neither is a trip limited to these three nations: the group also visits Chile between Uruguay and Bolivia, and the final part of the journey includes Peru.

The strongest contrast in the nature theme lies between Brazil's humid subtropics and Bolivia's Altiplano. On one journey, travelers see Iguaçu's powerful cascades and later find themselves among high-altitude lagoons, geysers, and the pale salt expanse of Uyuni. Uruguay adds a crossing of the estuary and a visit to Montevideo; neither program includes a separate nature tour through the country.

## Brazil: from Tijuca Forest to Iguaçu Falls

The Brazilian section of both itineraries includes Rio de Janeiro, Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain, and [Iguaçu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The drive to Corcovado passes through the green expanse of [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/), but the excursion itself focuses on city views and the Christ the Redeemer statue. A separate walk on forest trails would require additional time.

Brazil's main nature-focused day takes place on its side of Iguaçu. Water plunges over several powerful drops amid dense vegetation. Both tours include a group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide. The following day, travelers visit the Argentine side of the waterfalls before continuing to Buenos Aires.

The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are **optional excursions** on the Brazilian stage and must not be treated as included activities. This distinction matters when planning time: the principal waterfall walks already offer memorable natural scenery, while extending the sightseeing day requires separate arrangements.

## Uruguay: one day by ferry, not a coastal expedition

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited on an excursion from Buenos Aires. The group leaves early for the port, crosses the Río de la Plata by ferry, and spends the day in Uruguay's capital. The planned stops include the port, Independence Square, the old town, and the cathedral. Travelers return to Argentina after some free time.

This is **day eight of the 20-day tour and day nine of the 32-day tour**. Neither includes an overnight stay in Uruguay. The ferry crossing offers views of the broad estuary and urban waterfront, but there are no visits to nature reserves, marine wildlife-watching excursions, or walks on remote beaches in the itinerary.

Travelers whose main goal is to explore Uruguay's natural regions will need additional days. Here, Uruguay is a short cultural and sightseeing addition to a lengthy trip; the nature focus lies primarily in Brazil and Bolivia.

## Bolivia: lagoons, geothermal fields, and Uyuni

After sightseeing in Santiago and an overnight stay in [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), travelers cross into Bolivia and begin **a two-day journey in 4×4 vehicles**. The landscape changes dramatically: dry air, high plateaus, colored lagoons, and volcanic terrain.

Stops include [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Salvador Dalí Desert, Polques hot springs, the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The next day continues past the Honda, Hedionda, and Cañapa lagoons, the Ollagüe area, the Chiguana Salt Flat, and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). These stages alternate colored waters, mineral plains, and geothermal areas.

Here, the experience depends much more on altitude, cold, wind, and road conditions than on a short walk beside waterfalls. The itinerary includes time in San Pedro de Atacama for acclimatization as well as a specific warning about possible altitude sickness. The format involves long drives; it is neither a walking trek nor a specialist sporting expedition.

After Uyuni, the route includes a flight to La Paz and then a high-altitude journey toward Peru. The two-day Bolivian section cannot simply be “added” to a short Brazil–Uruguay holiday without consequences: an international border, roads, and subsequent flights link it to the rest of the itinerary.

## Two itineraries: what is the actual difference?

| | 20 days and 6 countries | 32 days and 8 countries |
|---|---|---|
| Brazil | Rio, Iguaçu | Rio, Iguaçu; starts with arrival in São Paulo |
| Uruguay | Montevideo excursion and return to Argentina | Same Montevideo visit arrangement |
| Bolivia | Two days among high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni, then La Paz | Similar highland section |
| After Bolivia | Peru, ending in Lima | Peru, then Ecuador with the Galápagos and Colombia |

Both programs include domestic flights, specified excursions, and accommodation in 4-star hotels. International flights are excluded. Full prices and dates are given on the [20-day](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [32-day](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) tour pages; the differences in duration and geography are more important than the total number of countries in this filter.

If nature is your primary interest, prepare for two very different sets of conditions. Spray protection and shoes with reliable grip are useful at the waterfalls; warm layers and protection from wind and sun are essential in the highlands. The Uruguay crossing depends on the ferry schedule, while Bolivia calls for readiness for long drives. These practicalities determine a comfortable travel pace.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are nature excursions included in all three countries?

No. The principal natural sights are Iguaçu in Brazil and the high-altitude lagoons, geothermal fields, and Uyuni in Bolivia. In Uruguay, the program consists of a ferry crossing and a sightseeing tour of Montevideo.

### Should I choose between 20 and 32 days because of Bolivia?

Both trips include a similar two-day highland section. The longer program also visits Ecuador and Colombia; overall duration, preferred countries, and time for nature excursions matter more when deciding.

### Are Macuco Safari and the Bird Park included?

They are offered separately on these tours. The main waterfall excursion is included, while additional activities require separate arrangements.

### Can a tour be organized for just these three countries?

Yes, an itinerary limited to these countries can be discussed as an individual program. Our existing tours, however, also travel through Argentina, Chile, and Peru; there is no ready-made shortened version covering only these three.

kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore wildlife along a route through Bolivia, Brazil, and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Nature experiences are unevenly distributed across itineraries featuring Bolivia, Brazil, and Uruguay. Brazil offers Tijuca Forest and Iguaçu Falls, while Bolivia has high-altitude lagoons with flamingos and the Uyuni Salt Flat. Uruguay features a one-day visit to Montevideo. Compare the 32-day wildlife-oriented tour with a 20-day scenic alternative.
---

## What you can actually see in the three countries

[Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Brazil](/brazil/), and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) appear in {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in Ada Tours' [“Wildlife and Safari”](/interests/wildlife/) theme. The selection currently includes a 32-day itinerary through 8 countries. This is **an overlap of countries within a much larger journey**, not three separate safaris: some wildlife experiences take place outside the selected trio. The 20-day journey through 6 countries mentioned below belongs to the “Nature” theme and is included as a landscape-focused alternative.

The principal nature section in Brazil features humid subtropical forest near Iguaçu and the green surroundings of Rio. In Bolivia, travelers enter a completely different environment: windswept highlands, mineral-rich lakes, and salt flats. Uruguay offers a city visit, and the program does not promise a dedicated wildlife-watching activity there.

| Country | Nature-focused part of the itinerary |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Tijuca, Iguaçu Falls |
| Bolivia | Lagoons, flamingos, Uyuni |
| Uruguay | Montevideo, city sightseeing day |

This is the distribution to consider when choosing a trip. If you want wildlife encounters in all three countries, the current selection of excursions would need separate discussion: a general thematic label does not add nature outings that the program never included.

## Brazil: from the forest above Rio to Iguaçu

In Rio, the route to Corcovado passes through [Tijuca Forest](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/). The main purpose of the excursion is the mountain, Christ the Redeemer, and views over the city. The forest is visible along the way, but neither itinerary includes a separate, full-length birdwatching or wildlife trail on this section.

The journey then continues to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Here, travelers can experience an extensive natural system: cascading water, islands, and forest along the riverbanks. Brazil's Iguaçu National Park protects part of the Atlantic Forest, important for regional biodiversity. However, the viewpoint excursion is principally a visit to the falls; sightings of particular animals cannot be guaranteed.

Our tours offer a visit to the [Bird Park near Iguaçu](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/), but this is **an optional excursion at additional cost**, not automatically included wildlife watching. If choosing between a waterfall walk and a visit to the Bird Park, check the timing immediately: both activities compete for the same excursion-day hours. For a more detailed comparison of Brazil's nature activities, explore [nature tours in Brazil](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/).

## Bolivia: flamingos at the lagoons and a high-altitude desert

Bolivia's nature section begins after [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile. Both longer tours include a two-day journey in 4×4 vehicles across the highlands toward [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Stops include [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Salvador Dalí Desert, Polques springs, and the Sol de Mañana geysers.

[Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) is particularly significant. Our itineraries mention James's flamingos, which use the shallow high-altitude lakes as feeding grounds. The following stages include the Honda, Chiar Khota, [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), and Cañapa lagoons, as well as salt flats on the way to Uyuni. This provides an opportunity to see strikingly different landscapes within a short time, although the concentration of birds varies and sightings depend on animal behavior and weather.

The decisive practical consideration is **altitude exceeding 4,000 m on some sections**. Long journeys on unpaved roads, dry air, cold mornings, and overnight stays in the desert require a different approach from sightseeing in Rio. The itineraries explicitly warn that altitude sickness may occur. Travelers with medical limitations should discuss this stage with a doctor before booking rather than expecting to resolve the issue on the road.

The Uyuni Salt Flat concludes this intensive nature section. Its principal appeal lies in its surface, light, and seemingly endless open space; visiting the salt flat does not in itself mean watching animals. Additional choices can be compared among [nature tours in Bolivia](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/).

## Uruguay: distinguishing a city day from wildlife watching

Both programs visit [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) by ferry from Buenos Aires and return to Argentina. Sightseeing covers the capital's historic streets and squares, including the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/).

The stop provides a break between major sightseeing sections and a chance to explore the culture of the opposite shore of the Río de la Plata. **Uruguay's national parks, coastal birdwatching, and expeditions to see marine animals are not listed in either of these two itineraries.** If Uruguay's wildlife is a primary motivation, the duration and content of this stage will need to change; a city day should not be treated as a nature tour.

## The 32-day wildlife route and the 20-day nature alternative

The [20-day tour through 6 countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) connects Rio, Iguaçu, a one-day Uruguay visit, Chile, Bolivia, and Peru. The natural highlights within the selected trio are Brazil's waterfalls and Bolivia's lagoons. The [32-day itinerary through 8 countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) retains those essential stops, then adds Ecuador and Colombia after Peru.

The 32-day program also includes **the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador**, with a sea excursion. This is a separate geographic stage and must not be counted among the attractions of Bolivia, Brazil, or Uruguay. The island-day itinerary follows either North Seymour with Bachas or South Plaza with Punta Carrión; both alternatives are not promised together.

The table below compares programs that include opportunities to observe wild animals or birds. Landscape-focused routes without such observations can be compared in the [nature travel selection](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_uruguay/interests/nature/). On a multi-country tour, wildlife encounters may take place outside the countries highlighted in the selection's title: check the full itinerary and its specific days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If you want to watch wildlife with fewer transfers, compare options in the [multi-country “Wildlife and Safari” catalog](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) or the general [Bolivia, Brazil, and Uruguay combination](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_uruguay/). Extending a route to reach one particular ecosystem is worthwhile only if the program allocates genuine excursion time to it.

## Preparing for this combination

In Brazil, comfortable shoes and protection for your belongings from spray at the falls matter most. Bolivia requires layered warm clothing, protection from sun and dust, and time to adjust to altitude; long drives between lagoons can be tiring. Uruguay's city day starts with an early ferry and ends back in Buenos Aires, so it is poorly suited to spontaneously adding a distant nature excursion.

When comparing specific departures, check the sequence of domestic flights and transfers, length of stops, guide languages, and list of optional activities. Tickets and services should match **the actual inclusions of the chosen tour**, not broad promises about the region. At places where wild birds and animals live, a sighting remains a matter of chance even when the visit itself is included.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife on a route through Bolivia, Brazil, and Uruguay

### Which of the three countries actually includes planned birdwatching?

Primarily Bolivia, where the route passes Laguna Colorada with its flamingos. In Brazil, the Bird Park near Iguaçu is an optional service. Neither of these tours includes a separate birdwatching program in Uruguay.

### Can I visit only Bolivia, Brazil, and Uruguay on the listed itineraries?

The existing programs cover more countries: one visits 6, the other 8. The selected trio is an overlap of their main countries, not a self-contained continuous tour restricted to these nations.

### Which stage requires the most physical preparation?

The high-altitude road section in Bolivia: some stops exceed 4,000 m and the overnight stay is in the desert. It is a jeep journey with stops, not a mountaineering expedition, but altitude can still have a significant effect on how you feel.

targetPath: /multi-country/bolivia_chile/
kind: multi_country_combination
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore journeys through Bolivia and Chile"
lead: >-
  Bolivia and Chile connect through the Uyuni Salt Flat, the colored lagoons of the Altiplano, and the Atacama Desert. Across a single border, the scenery changes from white salt and high-altitude volcanoes to the dry valleys around San Pedro de Atacama. The choice of border crossing, altitude, Uyuni's season, and time for onward travel to Santiago or Patagonia all play a decisive role in planning.
---

## Bolivia and Chile: two ways to build one journey

Bolivia and Chile can be combined in two fundamentally different ways. The first is **a continuous Altiplano route** linking [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), high-altitude lagoons in southwestern Bolivia, and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in northern Chile. The second is a wider itinerary that continues after the desert to [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and southern Chile, as far as [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/).

In both versions, the two countries are neighbors on a map, but the distances within them are vast. A large part of Chile lies between the high-altitude lagoons and Patagonia, requiring a separate transport stage. It is therefore misleading to estimate a trip's duration by the number of borders crossed: even a “Bolivia and Chile” tour can be more intensive than a three-country itinerary featuring brief city stops.

Our catalog contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It brings together trips in which **both countries form part of the main itinerary**, including programs that also visit Argentina, Peru, or other destinations. The exact stops are specified on each tour page.

## What to see between Uyuni and the Atacama

The white surface of [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is the Bolivian stage's most recognizable sight. Farther south, the terrain becomes more mountainous, with salt flats, volcanoes, and colored lagoons. [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) is known for its reddish water and flamingos, while [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) lies near Licancabur Volcano at the Chilean border.

After crossing the border, the journey often continues through San Pedro de Atacama. This is a convenient base for exploring the [Valley of the Moon](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/), salt flats, and volcanic landscapes of northern Chile. Some itineraries include the El Tatio geysers and nighttime astronomy experiences. Whether these outings form part of a specific tour must be checked in its program: proximity to San Pedro does not mean an excursion is included.

This section appeals to travelers looking for nature and unusual landscapes. The excursions differ from ordinary city walks: trips may begin before dawn, temperatures at altitude can be very low, and some stretches follow unpaved roads. Check the driver arrangements, vehicle type, meals, and excursion stops against the terms of the specific offer.

If you want to end your journey among southern glaciers and granite towers, another substantial transport stage must be added after northern Chile. The [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine area](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) has entirely different weather and walking arrangements. Patagonia cannot be treated as a short extension of an Atacama excursion.

## Choosing a tour

| Itinerary | Main difference |
|---|---|
| Bolivia + Chile, 16 days | Uyuni, Atacama, and Patagonia |
| Argentina + Chile + Bolivia, 12 days | Glaciers and Uyuni |
| Chile + Bolivia + Peru, 12 days | Atacama, Titicaca, Machu Picchu |

The [16-day private tour “Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile”](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) begins in La Paz and Uyuni, then travels past high-altitude lagoons to San Pedro de Atacama and Santiago. The final stage includes Chilean Patagonia. It suits travelers willing to devote more time to experiencing both northern and southern Chile on one itinerary.

The [12-day “Patagonia and Uyuni Salt Flat” tour](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/) starts in Buenos Aires, visits Perito Moreno Glacier and Torres del Paine, then heads toward Santiago and Bolivia's highlands. It is **a three-country program that includes Argentina**, not a short two-country tour.

The [“VIP Tour of Chile, Bolivia, and Peru”](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-vip/) travels in another direction: Santiago, San Pedro, Uyuni, La Paz, Titicaca, and Cusco in Peru. It is suited to travelers interested in the desert, Andean culture, and Machu Picchu together. This itinerary also covers three countries, and Peru's entry requirements must be checked separately.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_bolivia_chile_hidden_treasures_16_days,tour_source_prekrasnaya_patagoniya_i_solonchak_uyuni,tour_source_vip_tur_v_peru}}

When comparing itineraries, first find out how many **nights are spent at high altitude**, how many full days are allocated to Uyuni and the Atacama, and how many are used for transportation. A longer tour does not necessarily include more sights in every region: some extra days may be devoted to flights to Patagonia.

## The Uyuni–San Pedro de Atacama border crossing

For a route through the southern Bolivian lagoons, one established crossing is **Hito Cajón**, near San Pedro de Atacama. According to the official Chilean border crossings authority, it is situated at approximately **4,549 m** and is intended for cars and minibuses. Vehicle requirements and the feasibility of using the crossing must nevertheless be confirmed for the specific tour. You should not assume a large coach can cross on any chosen schedule.

The crossing's opening hours, weather-related closures, and road conditions can change. Roadblocks may also occur in Bolivia, making a check immediately before departure essential. If the trip involves a flight from Calama or Santiago, allow time after the high-altitude journey for border procedures, baggage collection, and the trip to the airport.

When entering Chile, travelers must comply with **SAG** rules on declaring products of animal and plant origin. These apply to personal luggage too: fruit, meat products, seeds, and other items may need to be declared and inspected. Removing unsuitable food from trail snacks beforehand is preferable to a dispute at border control. Passport control and sanitary requirements fall under different authorities.

If a conventional flight between the countries is needed, the route should be built around operating airports and available connections. Calama is the nearest major airport to San Pedro, while southern Chile requires further domestic flights and overland transfers. Never assume a direct service exists between particular cities without checking timetables for the travel dates.

## Entry and visas: Russian citizens

**According to official information checked on October 15, 2026**, Russian citizens holding a valid ordinary international passport may make short tourist trips to **Bolivia and Chile without a visa** for up to **90 days in each 180-day period** under the relevant bilateral agreements. The permitted periods in the two countries are calculated separately; visiting one does not remove the need for checks in the other.

When crossing at Hito Cajón, travelers must complete immigration formalities on both sides. Current conditions, document validity, possible proof of travel arrangements, and the rules of any transit countries must be verified for the specific passport. For example, an itinerary via Buenos Aires requires consideration of [Argentina](/argentina/) as a third country.

Conditions may differ for citizens of other countries. When planning a private or group trip, **each individual's passport** matters, not only the country from which the group departs. Special documents for minors and rules for traveling with one parent should be checked according to citizenship and the family's circumstances.

## Altitude and health: the most demanding part of the journey

The journey through Uyuni and the lagoons takes place at high altitude. La Paz lies at approximately 3,650 m, Uyuni at around 3,660 m, and the Hito Cajón border crossing is higher still. San Pedro de Atacama, by contrast, is considerably lower, at approximately 2,400 m. The difference is especially noticeable after flying from sea level or traveling quickly without intermediate acclimatization.

A gentler schedule is advisable for the first few days. Headache, nausea, and unusual weakness can indicate altitude sickness. Worsening symptoms require medical assessment and stopping further ascent; physical fitness alone does not prevent the effects of altitude. Travelers with heart or lung conditions should discuss the itinerary with a doctor before buying tickets.

Before booking, make sure insurance covers the actual altitude reached and medical evacuation from remote locations. Adequate warm clothing, water, UV protection, and the flexibility to change plans in bad weather are also essential. Visits to lagoons and geysers call for different preparation from sightseeing around Santiago.

## When to go: mirror-like Uyuni and Patagonia's seasons

Bolivia and Chile do not share one universal “best month.” In drier periods, Uyuni shows a white salt surface; during the rainy season, a layer of water can sometimes reflect the sky, but it also restricts travel along some routes. **The mirror effect cannot be guaranteed on any particular date.**

The Atacama is an extremely dry desert, but that does not mean it is always warm: nights, particularly at altitude, are cold. Farther south, conditions change. Strong winds, rain, and rapid weather shifts are possible in Patagonia even in summer. For walks and longer visits in Torres del Paine, many travelers choose the southern summer, approximately November to March, while recognizing that conditions remain changeable.

| Region | What to consider |
|---|---|
| Uyuni | Rain affects road access |
| Atacama | Cold nights at altitude |
| Patagonia | Wind and rapidly changing weather |

An itinerary through Uyuni, Atacama, and Patagonia requires several types of clothing: warm layers for dawn and high-altitude sections, sun protection, and a windproof, waterproof outer layer for the south. Check baggage allowances for every flight, particularly if several local airlines are involved.

## Money, payments, and communications

Bolivia uses the **boliviano (BOB)** and Chile uses the **Chilean peso (CLP)**. US dollars are useful as backup currency for exchanging money, but they cannot always be used directly to pay in shops or hotels. Local-currency cash is particularly useful in remote Bolivian areas, whereas card payments are more common in large Chilean cities.

**Russian-issued Visa and Mastercard cards do not work abroad.** If you have a bank card issued in another country, check its issuer, fees, limits, and whether transactions actually work in both destinations before departure. Carry a modest reserve of locally permitted cash for both sides of the border day: ATMs and exchange desks cannot be relied upon at a remote high-altitude crossing.

Remember mobile connectivity and local time as well. Chile has seasonal clock changes, so after arrival it is wise to reconfirm transfer and flight boarding times in the relevant local time zone. Offline maps, saved documents, and the organizer's contact details are helpful where mobile data is unreliable.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I travel overland from Uyuni to the Atacama?

Yes, many programs use the Hito Cajón border crossing area. However, this is a high-altitude crossing with vehicle restrictions and possible weather closures. Confirm the precise travel arrangements, operating hours, and onward road to San Pedro de Atacama for your itinerary dates.

### Do Russian citizens need visas for Bolivia and Chile?

For short tourist visits using a valid ordinary Russian international passport, official information checked on October 15, 2026 describes visa-free entry for up to 90 days within 180 days for each country. Transit and any third-country requirements must be checked separately.

### When is the Uyuni Salt Flat mirror-like?

In the rainy season, a thin layer of water sometimes forms and reflects the sky. Some roads may then be closed or accessible only on a modified route. The effect depends on actual water and weather conditions, not on a promise based on the calendar.

### How much time is needed for Bolivia, Atacama, and Patagonia?

Choose an extended itinerary for all three: these are remote regions that require flights and overland travel between them. The [16-day Bolivia + Chile program](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) includes both Atacama and Patagonia. With less time, focusing on Uyuni and northern Chile is sensible.

### Can I carry food across the border into Chile?

Chile requires declarations for certain products of plant or animal origin, including food in personal backpacks. Check SAG requirements before crossing; some items must be declared or cannot be imported.

### Will the same clothes work for Uyuni and Patagonia?

You will need layers for both, but the weather differs: high-altitude nights are cold and daytime sun is intense, while southern Chile can be windy and rainy. All clothing must also fit within the baggage allowances of the actual flights.

## Bolivia and Chile: what kind of adventure awaits across the border?

This pair of countries has a recognizable natural corridor: the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the colored lagoons of Bolivia's Altiplano, a crossing of the Andes, and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). In photographs, these sights may seem like a chain of neighboring attractions. On the ground, they are separated by hours of travel at high altitude, stretches without familiar city infrastructure, and distinct border formalities.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which Bolivia and Chile are both on the main route and adventure is a primary or secondary interest. **That label does not mean every tour includes a multi-day hike.** Some trips cross the Altiplano by four-wheel-drive vehicle; others add national parks and southern lakes after the Atacama; and longer sightseeing tours also visit Peru, Argentina, or Brazil. For an overall comparison of the logistics, consult the [Bolivia and Chile travel catalog](/multi-country/bolivia_chile/). Here, the focus is on actual exertion and adventure activities.

## Uyuni, lagoons, and Atacama: an off-road adventure

In Bolivia, the central natural stop is [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The salt flat looks very different when dry and after rain, when water in some areas reflects the sky. Planning an entire trip solely around the “mirror” effect is risky: water levels, accessible sections, and weather all change. The driver determines the exact path across the salt flat according to current conditions.

The route then passes the Altiplano lagoons, sometimes including the area around [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the Sol de Mañana geysers, and the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). The value of this journey lies in the remoteness of the scenery and the succession of salt flats, volcanic plateaus, and colorful lakes. At the same time, it is the most demanding section in terms of time buffers, clothing, and wellbeing at altitude.

In Chile, the terrain changes to Atacama's volcanic valleys, salt flats, and [El Tatio geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/). Check which sites are included in the core days of a specific tour and which are separate excursions. An early departure for the geysers and an evening visit to the Valley of the Moon, for example, take place at different times and call for different clothing.

**The main distinction:** this is primarily an off-road high-altitude adventure with stops at viewpoints. If you are looking for a genuine walking trek lasting several days, it should not be equated with trekking simply because it carries the word “adventure.”

## What if you continue on to Patagonia?

On the [16-day “Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile” tour](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/), the route continues after Uyuni and the Atacama via Santiago to [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), then on to San Rafael Glacier and the [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/). The final stages also include a winery and Valparaíso. This means choosing **two major natural regions** — the Altiplano and Patagonia — with flights and long overland journeys between them.

This sequence suits those who want to experience both the dry northern landscapes and the glacier country of the south. But the southern stages are not a continuation of the same jeep tour: temperatures, winds, road types, and the risk of weather restrictions on boat excursions are different. Clothes suitable for warm Santiago will not replace insulation and a waterproof outer layer in Patagonia.

In [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), distinguish a vehicle-based overview of the park from a mountain hike. An extended trek needs additional days, access to permitted trails, and sometimes accommodation along the way. Merely including the park in a program does not mean the W or O circuit is completed.

## Altitude matters more than sporting experience

Travelers stay overnight at considerable elevation in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), and some Altiplano sections are higher still. The speed of ascent and the order of overnight stops affect the risk of altitude sickness; good physical fitness alone does not remove it. Pay particular attention to programs that arrive in the highlands and almost immediately continue toward the lagoons.

Discuss the actual accommodation altitudes, the pace of the first days, the option of a more relaxed start, time buffers, and transport arrangements with us. Travelers with chronic conditions should make decisions about the suitability of high-altitude exertion in consultation with a doctor. That discussion matters more than choosing a trip based on a beautiful photograph of the salt flat.

## Border, weather, and money in practice

When crossing between Bolivia's Altiplano and Chile, **check both countries' immigration requirements for each traveler's citizenship**, as well as any transit through a third country included in the route. An overland crossing and an arrival by air are different transport scenarios. Chile also has rules on declaring plant and animal products in luggage, including food taken for the journey; a non-commercial purpose does not remove the declaration requirement.

Bolivia uses the boliviano, and Chile uses the Chilean peso. Having US dollars does not guarantee that every purchase in a remote area can be paid for with them; the actual usability of a particular bank card should also be checked before departure. Agree in advance which expenses are covered by the program, where local currency will be needed, and what backup payment method is available.

Cold, windy mornings, intense sun, and dry air are common on the road, with Patagonia's weather added if you choose to continue south. Warm layers, sun protection, drinking water, and shoes suitable for stepping safely onto uneven ground are useful for the off-road stages. Follow current opening hours and restrictions in the parks: trail access changes with the weather, so a time buffer is more valuable than a promise that every trail can be completed.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Bolivia and Chile

### Do I need serious trekking experience for the Uyuni–Atacama route?

For most of the jeep itineraries described here, multi-day walking experience is not the main focus. But high altitude, transfers, rough roads, and weather can still be physically tiring. Check exactly which walks are involved and the elevations of overnight stops.

### Can Uyuni and Torres del Paine be combined in one journey?

Yes. The [16-day Bolivia–Chile itinerary](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) includes Uyuni and southern Patagonia. That requires extra flights and days between the natural areas; the program has no short direct overland transfer connecting them.

### When does Uyuni have a mirror-like surface?

The effect depends on water on the salt flat and on weather conditions, so no fixed calendar date can guarantee reflections. When planning, discuss which matters most: mirror views, access to more areas, or the overall Altiplano route.

### Can I visit only Bolivia and Chile without Peru?

Yes. The selection includes a [standalone two-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/). Some other tours, however, include Peru as a main country. The actual itinerary determines the journey, not the two names shown in the selected filter.

### What happens if weather closes a mountain trail or boat excursion?

The exact procedure for alternatives and rescheduling depends on the terms of the chosen tour. We help arrange the sequence of transfers and possible time buffers, while access to trails and waterways is determined by current local rules. We cannot promise that a hazardous section will operate when it is closed.
